title: Reaction
description: A Reaction is a special action taken in response to a trigger defined in the Reaction’s description, which you can take on any turn. Once you take a Reaction, you can’t take another one until the start of your next turn.

contents.name: Cast a Spell
contents.summary: You can cast a spell with a casting time of a Reaction in response to a trigger that is defined in the spell’s Casting Time entry.

contents.name: Hit Surface Head or Feet First
contents.summary: In response to falling into water or another liquid (see Hazards > Falling), you make a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check to attempt to hit the surface head or feet first. On a successful check, any damage resulting from the fall is halved.

contents.name: Opportunity Attack
contents.summary: When a creature that you can see leaves your reach using an action or one of its speeds, you make one melee attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike against the provoking creature. The attack occurs right before the creature leaves your reach.

contents.name: Readied Action or Movement
contents.summary:
When the trigger of your previous Ready action occurs, you can either take your specified Reaction right after the trigger finishes (which can be an action or moving up to your Speed) or ignore the trigger.

To ready a spell, it must have a casting time of an action, and you must maintain Concentration. If your Concentration is broken, the spell dissipates without taking effect.
